articles.title: Meerut Outrage: BA Student Molested Near School, Accused Beaten by Crowd in Viral Video
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Meerut (Uttar Pradesh) – A shocking case of molestation has surfaced in TP Nagar, where a BA student was allegedly harassed and threatened by a man from her locality.

body.html:
Meerut (Uttar Pradesh) – A shocking case of molestation has surfaced in TP Nagar, where a BA student was allegedly harassed and threatened by a man from her locality. The incident took place on Monday afternoon (8 September) near BK School, when the student was returning home with friends.

According to the complaint filed by her father, the accused blocked her path, forced her to talk, and when she resisted, he beat and threatened to kill her while trying to pull her. The student somehow managed to escape and reach home.

Police have registered a case and launched a search for the accused. SP City Ayush Vikram Singh confirmed that officers are also reviewing CCTV footage from the area for evidence.

Meanwhile, a viral video from Nai Basti Colony shows the accused being caught by locals and brutally thrashed. In the clip, several women can be seen pulling his hair and scratching him, while others tore off his shirt and beat him. Eventually, he was taken away on a motorbike by two men before police intervention.

articles.title: Nepal Erupts: Finance Minister Stripped, Chased Into River Amid Anti-Corruption Protests
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Kathmandu – In a shocking turn of events, Nepal’s Finance Minister was stripped of his clothes and chased into a river by furious protesters during ongoing anti-corruption demonstrations.

body.html:
Kathmandu – In a shocking turn of events, Nepal’s Finance Minister was stripped of his clothes and chased into a river by furious protesters during ongoing anti-corruption demonstrations. The protests, which have already turned deadly, reflect the growing public anger over alleged large-scale corruption within the government.

Eyewitnesses reported that the minister was cornered by a mob before being forced to flee. The humiliating episode highlights the intensity of the unrest, which has spread across several regions.

Authorities have tightened security, but the situation remains volatile as public outrage against corruption continues to escalate.

articles.title: Job Scam Exposed: One Man Drew ₹4.5 Crore Salary from 6 Govt Posts! 💥
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A massive fraud has been unearthed in the Health Department. Arpit Singh, using the same identity, managed to secure government jobs in six different districts and drew a total salary of ₹4.5 crore over nine years.

body.html:
A massive fraud has been unearthed in the Health Department. Arpit Singh, using the same identity, managed to secure government jobs in six different districts and drew a total salary of ₹4.5 crore over nine years.

Investigations revealed that in 2016, Singh was appointed simultaneously in six districts through the Subordinate Services Selection Commission. The CBI probe has exposed how corruption had deeply infected the recruitment system. According to findings, slips were distributed in exchange for bribes, with political influence playing a key role.

Shockingly, one individual was officially employed in multiple districts at the same time.

articles.title: Churu Youth Rides Bike Into Hospital Ward, Saves Elderly Train Passenger
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Churu – In a remarkable act of humanity, a 28-year-old man rushed a critically ill passenger straight into the emergency ward of DB Hospital on his motorbike, saving the elderly man’s life.

body.html:
Churu – In a remarkable act of humanity, a 28-year-old man rushed a critically ill passenger straight into the emergency ward of DB Hospital on his motorbike, saving the elderly man’s life.

The patient, 65-year-old Bhalleram of Fatehabad, Haryana, was travelling with his family from Bikaner to Delhi after visiting Baba Ramdev when he suddenly collapsed inside the train near Churu. A diabetic, his blood sugar levels had dropped, leaving him unconscious and unresponsive.

Panicked, his son Ran Singh pulled the chain to stop the train. At that moment, Shubham Devda, who had come to drop his friend at the station, noticed the commotion. Without hesitation, he seated Bhalleram on his bike and drove directly into the hospital’s emergency ward—much like a scene from the film Three Idiots.

Doctors and nurses quickly shifted the patient to a bed and began treatment. Tests confirmed a severe drop in blood sugar as the cause of his collapse. Thanks to the swift response, Bhalleram’s condition stabilized.

Medical College Principal Dr. MM Pukar praised Shubham’s selfless act, calling it “an inspiring example of humanity.” He appealed to the public to extend similar help in emergencies, stressing that timely assistance can save lives.

#Churu #HumanityFirst #LifeSaved #ViralStory #RajasthanNews #InspiringAct #GoodSamaritan
